title: Telemetry-gated egress and soft-queue for SLO-driven active-active failover
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: We need a telemetry-driven egress controller and soft-queue layer at the edge/gateway to enable predictable active-active failover behavior that preserves streaming/session continuity where possible while meeting regional SLOs. The feature should allow region-level proportional dialing (reduce egress to a region gradually), transparent circuit gating for degraded region capacity, and a short-lived soft-queue for transient backpressure to avoid hard drops during bursts. This ticket covers the design, initial implementation, canary, and rollout plan for the hosted API edge.

Motivation: During multi-region capacity events we currently perform coarse traffic drains or instant failovers which cause many streaming sessions to abort and downstream apps to experience token loss. We need a mechanism to: 1) protect SLOs by shedding load in a controlled way, 2) avoid mass session termination where feasible, and 3) surface clear telemetry for automated decisioning.

Design overview:
- Egress controller: policy-engine placed in the regional gateway that subscribes to real-time telemetry (latency percentiles, tail latency P99.9, error rates, available GPU headroom, queue depth). Policies evaluate SLO headroom and produce an egress throttle factor per region (0.0-1.0).
- Soft-queue: small in-edge in-memory FIFO with per-session token cap (configurable, default 256 tokens) and short TTL (default 5s). When downstream model endpoints show transient overload the soft-queue accepts some inflight tokens to smooth spikes. If the queue fills, we escalate to circuit gating.
- Circuit gating: three-state regional circuit (CLOSED -> PROBATION -> OPEN). Transition rules use composite signals (error ratio, sustained P99, KV-cache miss surge). PROBATION allows a low QPS ramp with probing requests. OPEN routes a fraction of traffic to fallback variants or remote regions per routing rules.
- Session/stream preservation: for streaming sessions we attempt token-preserving reroutes: the gateway serializes the last KV window and issues a resume token placed in the routed request header. If resume cannot be honored (incompatible model or quantization mismatch) the gateway falls back to safe redirect with explicit session termination metadata.

Telemetry and decisioning:
- Required signals: per-region P50/P95/P99/P99.9 latency for generation and for connection handshake, total inflight tokens, model-level error counts (>=5xx and application-level decode errors), GPU utilization per pool, KV cache hit ratio, and per-session byte counts.
- Decision cadence: policy evaluation runs every 500ms with exponential backoff on repeated changes to reduce oscillation. Rate limits on policy changes will be enforced by the egress controller (min 2s between aggressive uplifts).

Acceptance criteria:
- A canary in one region that reduces soft-failover stream aborts by >=60% during a simulated GPU overload while keeping region P99 latency within SLO 95% of the time.
- Circuit opens only after two independent signals (latency spike plus error ratio) and yields a measurable drop in error rate in 30s.
- Soft-queue respects per-session token cap and evicts with clear telemetry event tags when TTL expires.
- Rollout tooling to pin a route to the new egress controller and to disable the soft-queue (kill-switch) remotely.

Implementation plan:
1) Build lightweight policy engine prototype in gateway (feature flagged). Integrate with existing metrics stream (Prometheus push/consumer pipeline) and a new low-latency telemetry topic in Kafka for headroom signals.
2) Implement soft-queue store with memory-optimized ring buffer per connection (C++ native path) and Node/Go control plane hooks.
3) Implement circuit state machine and probes. Add tracing hooks to Console (trace linking and per-request decision tags).
4) Add resume-token header format and resume compatibility checks in model adapter layer.
5) Canary in us-west-2 behind a controlled percentage of traffic with progressively stricter probes; gather dashboards and SLO impact.

Open tradeoffs:
- Memory vs latency: per-session soft-queue consumes memory; we limit to N sessions with guardrails and prefer eviction over blocking.
- Token continuity guarantees: full token-perfect resume requires model snapshotting support; we will implement best-effort resume with explicit fallbacks to avoid incorrect continuations.
- Oscillation risk: aggressive automatic dialing can oscillate; mitigation includes rate-limited policy changes and hysteresis windows.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Telemetry+Gated+Egress
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-gateway/pull/842
- Dashboard (canary): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/edge/egress-canary
- Incident runbook draft: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1Egxz-egress-runbook

Next steps: finalize policy DSL, implement soft-queue prototype, and schedule canary in cycle 2026-W10.
